findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence gene: tumour-up at protein [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269] and RNA [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312], replicated in TCGA kidney tumour-vs-normal [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712]. The signal survives purity extrapolation and drugs exist (girentuximab antibody, phase 3), but it is not prognostic in TCGA.

Safety flag: CA9 protein is tissue-enriched in a vital organ (stomach) in the GTEx proteome, with a tissue-specificity score of [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19], above the enrichment threshold. This is an on-target off-tumour concern for cytotoxic CA9 modalities, and no selective ccRCC dependency was found in DepMap.

CD70 is protein-confirmed up in tumour [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], replicates in TCGA, is tumour-intrinsic by purity, and has antibody programmes in clinical stages. It has no vital-organ enrichment in the GTEx proteome, with a low tissue-specificity score of [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34], making it a cleaner surface target than CA9.

ENPP3 is a membrane enzyme with protein up in tumour [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544], RNA and TCGA replication, tumour-intrinsic by purity, and an antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F, phase 2). It ranks high in the target profile but has no prognostic signal.

NNMT is strongly up at protein [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], tumour-intrinsic and replicated in TCGA. Higher expression predicts worse overall survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], so it is both a prognostic biomarker and a metabolic target, although it is cytosolic and has no approved drug.

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile (up in tumour, replicated in TCGA, tumour-intrinsic), but its protein is tissue-enriched in a vital organ (adrenal gland) with a tissue-specificity score of [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08]. This is a safety liability that tempers its target rank, and it has no drug or DepMap dependency.

ALDOB reflects loss of proximal tubule identity: it is down at protein [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-2.273] and far more at RNA [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-7.028]. Lower expression is also associated with worse survival in TCGA [gene=ALDOB; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.358]; it is a diagnostic or prognostic marker, not a target.

ALDH6A1 is a down-regulated metabolic gene with a frequent copy-number loss and a positive cis effect, and with the strongest favourable prognostic association in the biomarker shortlist: higher expression predicts better survival [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]. It is a prognostic tissue-loss biomarker, not a target.

Negative result: FCER1G looks strongly tumour-up in bulk, but its expression tracks purity inversely [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692], and extrapolated to a pure tumour the RNA change shrinks to [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061]. The signal is largely immune infiltration, not tumour-cell expression, so it is not a tumour-intrinsic target (the same pattern applies to TYROBP).

VHL is the disease mechanism gene: the short arm of chromosome 3 is lost in a large majority of tumours ([gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791]), with significant somatic recurrence and a positive cis dosage effect on its own RNA. VHL itself is not a drug target, and its loss explains the HIF-driven up-regulation of CA9, ANGPTL4 and related genes.

caveats: CPTAC discovery cohort is small (110 tumours; 75 RNA and 84 protein normals) and bulk tissue, so stromal and immune contributions need the purity check.

DepMap shows no selective ccRCC dependency for the leading up-regulated candidates (CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1), and 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology, so dependency evidence is absent rather than negative proof.
GTEX proteome excludes kidney and has detection limits; absence of normal expression is not proof of safety.
Down-regulated genes (ALDOB, ALDH6A1) reflect loss of tubule identity and are biomarker candidates only.
Rankings are deterministic composites; literature and drug streams favour well-studied genes (CA9, CD70) over novel ones (ENPP3, SCARB1).
